title: Budget-sensitive first-home couple
buyer_primary_need: Find an affordable, practical Type A 900 sq.ft. first home for a couple and young child, while understanding monthly payments, downpayment/upfront costs, and whether the layout will feel spacious enough.
key_information_learned: The buyer is purchasing for own stay with their spouse and young child.
Their comfortable budget is around RM3xxk; monthly instalment and downpayment matter.
They are concerned 900 sq.ft. may feel tight when furnished.
One carpark is sufficient for now.
The spouse is a joint decision-maker and needs to attend a viewing.
They want to see the Type A layout/unit and understand upfront costs.
important_information_missed: A verified itemized breakdown of additional upfront costs was not available.
The buyer had not confirmed a visit time; their spouse still needed to check availability.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: The pricing materials show base prices from RM328k. The package document lists an 8% rebate for some unit categories, which would make that base about RM302k before confirming the exact unit and current package validity. Are you looking for your own stay or as an investment?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Own stay, for me, my spouse and our young child. Is the 900 sqft Type A layout practical for a small family?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: For you, your spouse and your young child, the 900 sqft Type A looks practical on paper: it has 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms, with an efficient layout and little wasted corridor space. The living, dining and kitchen area is about 405 sqft; the project materials describe all three bedrooms as able to fit a queen bed, though furniture and circulation are worth checking against the actual layout. Would you want one room kept flexible for play or work?

transcript.message: Maybe one room can be for our child/play area for now. I’m still a bit worried 900 sqft might feel tight once we furnish it. transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
Yes—the RM302k figure is the current Type A package reference from for the 1-carpark category, not a price for every Type A unit. Floor, facing and the specific unit can change the final price, so I’d treat it as an entry reference until the exact unit is confirmed.

For a rough cash-flow illustration, assuming 90% financing over 35 years at 4.2%, the estimated monthly principal-and-interest payment is about RM1,245 at RM302k or RM1,352 at RM328k. At 90% financing, the 10% downpayment would be about RM30,200 or RM32,800 respectively, before fees—and the loan terms and eligibility would need to be confirmed with a bank.

On the space, the living/dining/kitchen area is about 405 sq ft, and the project materials describe the bedrooms as able to fit a queen bed. Furniture layout can still affect how roomy it feels, so it’s worth checking the actual plan. Would one carpark suit your household, or do you need two?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: One carpark should be enough for us for now. The monthly estimate sounds more manageable, but we’d need to understand the downpayment and other upfront costs before deciding. Could we see the actual Type A layout or unit to judge the space, and get a breakdown of the costs? My spouse would need to come too.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Yes—seeing the actual Type A layout together should help you judge the space. I’ll have my colleague coordinate a visit for both of you and prepare an upfront-cost breakdown based on the one-carpark Type A reference. The final figures will depend on the selected unit and applicable financing terms.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, thanks. Could you send a couple of available visit slots and the upfront-cost breakdown for the 1-carpark Type A? I’ll check which time works for my spouse too.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: I can’t verify specific open visit slots because the appointment calendar isn’t connected. The viewing reference says the Type A show unit can be viewed by appointment on Saturday or Sunday, 10:00 am–5:00 pm, subject to gallery confirmation; no time is held or confirmed. For the one-carpark Type A, the available price reference starts at RM302,000. Assuming 90% financing, 10% down would be about RM30,200 before fees. I don’t have a verified itemized breakdown of other upfront costs, and financing terms aren’t confirmed.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Thanks, that’s helpful. I’ll check with my spouse—weekend 10am–5pm could work, but I can’t confirm a time yet. Could you send the Type A floor plan and any verified upfront-cost items you do have, even if it’s not a full breakdown?

judge.summary: Yes. In this run, Human Support supplied verified answers to two distinct operational questions, and the AI retained ownership, resumed in customer-facing language, applied the payment and pricing answers to the buyer's budget concern, and continued selling rather than merely relaying results. It recognized genuine viewing readiness and correctly handed off operational booking with LOW sales work remaining. The appointment was not confirmed: the buyer still needed to check with their spouse, and the human could not verify an open slot. The human response also did not complete the requested slot check or provide an itemized upfront-cost breakdown. The support fixtures are simulator-only verified evidence, not Pearlmont factual Knowledge or evidence of a live production system.
judge.improvement_recommendation: For simple price enquiries, lead with the retrieved effective package entry-price guidance and explain uncertainty about category and current validity without opening on the base price. After a support-backed affordability answer, continue as done here: relate the numbers to the buyer's stated comfort range, state assumptions, and connect layout uncertainty to viewing. At handoff, make the outstanding operational tasks explicit—slot confirmation and any verified upfront-cost items—without implying they are already available.
